author: P. N. Evans
title: Senator Katie Boyd Britt highlights defense priorities and legislative actions in June 2026 posts
text:
Senator Katie Boyd Britt, a U.S. Senator from Alabama and chair of the homeland security appropriations subcommittee, shared several updates on June 10, 2026, regarding national security, border protection, and judicial nominations.
In her first post at 15:14 UTC, Britt wrote: “We have to make sure our military is the best trained, equipped, and ready across the planet. We need to support @POTUS so he can finish the job in Iran with precision, and we can ensure that Americans are kept safe from a regime that wishes to do us harm.”
Later that day at 16:09 UTC, she commented on new legislation signed by the President: “.@POTUS just signed the Secure America Act into law providing $70 billion for our security and safety through the end of his term. Republicans are proud to stand with the hardworking men and women of ICE and Border Patrol and to continue putting the American people FIRST.”
At 17:10 UTC, Britt acknowledged a judicial nominee from her home state: “It was an honor to support my dear friend and Montgomery native Kasdin Mitchell’s nomination to be a U.S. District Judge this morning. Kasdin’s intellect, integrity, grit, and commitment to service have made Alabama so proud. I have no doubt that when confirmed, she will serve”
According to her official website, Britt supports Alabamians through coordination with federal agencies and nominations for service academies ( https://www.britt.senate.gov/ ). She advocates for family values, economic opportunities, social media safeguards for minors, mental health access policies, educational options for youth, agricultural aid programs, and national security measures. In addition to chairing the homeland security appropriations subcommittee, Britt also serves on Senate committees covering appropriations, judiciary matters, banking housing and urban affairs, as well as rules and administration. Before her election to the Senate she served as president of Alabama’s business council.
